title: Clawdbot to Moltbot to OpenClaw: The 72 Hours That Broke Everything (The Full Breakdown)

hook_anatomy.first_5_seconds: In hundreds of cities across the globe right now, developers are queuing up to buy Mac Minis, specifically to give an AI agent root access to their digital life
hook_anatomy.emotional_trigger: urgency and mystery around global tech phenomenon

act_breakdown.description: Mystery setup - global Mac Mini buying frenzy and stock movements
Product explanation and explosive growth story
The 72-hour crisis - legal issues, security breaches, scams
Deep technical security analysis and architectural flaws
Why it's popular despite risks and future implications

It's safe because it's neutered. Maultbot is useful because it's dangerous

content_patterns.primary_topic: AI agent security and adoption analysis

key_quotes: AI that actually does things. That's not marketing fluff. It is the core value prop and the core risk condensed into five words

we spent twenty years essentially building security boundaries around our OSes, and everything that we've done is designed to contain and limit scope of action. But agents require us to tear that down
Running multbot safely largely defeats the purpose of multbot because a sandboxed assistant can't access your real email and calendar
analysis.one_line_summary: A deep investigation into how MoltBot became GitHub's fastest-growing project while exposing massive security vulnerabilities that reveal the fundamental tension between AI agent capability and safety.
